rationale: This is a mechanical product of two already-tested archive signals (direction-consistency intensity and intangible opacity) with no new economic ingredient, and the triple multiplication of a coarse {1/3,1} consistency weight by an intangible rank that is near-zero for most hard-asset firms will shrink the signal toward a thin, intangible-heavy subsample rather than genuinely test complementarity.

The conditioner shifts from the quantity of real investment (all prior archive variants) to its profitability per unit of installed capital, the expression matches the stated hypothesis and the expected negative sign follows naturally from a signed accrual intensity times a non-negative deterioration rank, though ib/ppent changes will be noisy for asset-light firms.

The sequencing idea (prior-year accrual bloat followed by a capex cut) is genuinely new relative to the archive's contemporaneous conditioners and the expression is internally consistent, but the extra LAG stales the accrual signal by a full year, which likely costs much of the known accrual decay, and capex growth is itself close to the abnormal-investment anomaly.

The conditioner is close to mechanically induced by the numerator — building non-cash working capital is largely financed by drawing down cash, so NEG(Δche/at) and the WC accrual are two components of the same funding identity (and both are components of total accruals in Richardson et al.), making the "resilience" interpretation unidentified from a tautological overlap.

The hypothesis is about inventory unmatched by *trade credit*, but the expression subtracts the change in all non-debt current liabilities (accrued expenses, taxes payable, deferred revenue, etc.), so the computed quantity is essentially a re-labelled working-capital accrual rather than the supplier-financing test claimed — use Δap if that is the mechanism.

This is the same two ingredients and the same interaction as the already-tested AccrualBloatWithoutCapitalReplacement (and its MIN variant), differing only in replacing IND_RANK of the accrual with its winsorized signed level — a textbook cosmetic re-specification, and the diagnostic question about the FMB/alpha sign conflict would be better addressed by examining portfolio composition and nonlinearity than by re-running the same product.
